What makes our cheese different
starts on our farm.

SEASONAL GRAZING

Our cows and our cheese change with the seasons.

Our family and a handful of loyal employees live here with our herd of 150 cows, surrounded by 500 acres of pasture. For the length of each year's grazing season, we transform grass into milk into cheese.

HANDMADE CHEESE

Pastures, cows and caves, all in one place.

Every morning, milk runs seventy feet underground, from our milking barn right into our cheese vat.

CAVE-AGED

Natural rinds give our cheese a taste of place.

Months of care in open-air caves bring our cheeses to their fullest expression.

From the farm

A working family farm.

Our farm sits on Pleasant Ridge, in the Driftless Region of southwest Wisconsin. Untouched by glaciers, these karst hills hold some of the world's finest grazing soils.

Our crossbred cows calve in the spring, when the grass comes up, and rotate onto fresh pasture twice every day until the snow comes. Each morning of our 200-day grazing season, we make a single batch of cheese, distilling that day's pasture and reflecting the unique character of our pastures and cows.

Alpine-style · Aged 9+ months

Pleasant Ridge Reserve

Made in the tradition of alpine-style cheeses like Gruyère and Beaufort, Pleasant Ridge Reserve is a direct reflection of the 10 acres of pasture our herd grazed the previous day. Each batch has slightly different attributes depending on a variety of factors, such as the weather, what kind of plants the cows were grazing, and the natural, seasonal fluctuations of our milk's composition.

Pleasant Ridge Reserve is most often identified by its characteristically sweet profile that can best be compared to caramel or toffee, but comes balanced out with other attributes like tropical fruit, savory or broth-like notes, or a roasted, nutty character. Since each batch reflects a different section of land the cows grazed upon, it becomes a window into that day in time — the weather, the land and the cows themselves. Once the cheesemaking process has transformed the milk into wheels of cheese, we patiently wait for upwards of a year while our team diligently washes and tends to the cheeses in our caves, hoping to coax out the best characteristics of each batch.

Pleasant Ridge, like its European inspirations, is an extremely versatile cheese, as at home on a cheese plate as it is melted into your favorite dish. We are especially fond of using it in gratins, French onion soups, fondues, or melted into a luxurious grilled cheese sandwich. It pairs well with crisp white wines or lighter-bodied reds, as well as most any wheat or Belgian beers. If serving on a cheese board, we love playing against Pleasant Ridge Reserve's sweet and nutty profile by pairing it with contrasting flavors — dark chocolate, charcuterie, or pickled items are all great combos to accentuate the character of the cheese while providing balance.

CARE & SERVICE

Storage & Serving

Keep refrigerated at 38–42°F. Bring to room temperature before serving. Pleasant Ridge Reserve can be stored for several weeks but is at its peak within a couple of weeks of its receiving date. Rush Creek Reserve is meant to be enjoyed as a young cheese and should be consumed by the best-by date printed on the label of the wheel.

Shipping information

We ship perishable cheese carefully, on your schedule.

We ship anywhere in the United States for a flat $20 per order; orders of only gift boxes, prints or merchandise ship free. We cannot ship internationally. Orders ship Monday through Wednesday to avoid weekend transit delays, and orders placed after 12PM Central on Tuesday ship the following week. In your cart, you can select a preferred delivery week for your cheese. Need it more quickly or need to delay? Email or call us and we'll do our best to accommodate what you need.

How it works

What to expect when you order from us.

We ship anywhere in the United States. Shipping is a flat $20 per order, and orders of only gift boxes, prints or merchandise ship free.

Due to the perishable nature of our cheese, we only ship Monday through Wednesday to avoid weekend delays. Orders placed after 12PM Central on Tuesday will automatically ship the following week unless you choose a later delivery week in your cart.

For seasonal products like Rush Creek Reserve, we are constrained by availability and supply, as the cheese is only delivered during a short season: the weeks of November 2 through December 28. We are able to ship on your preferred timeline when the product is available, but when it's sold out, we will not be able to fulfill any additional orders.

Questions about your order? Call us at 608-935-5558 or email orders@uplandscheese.com.

Dodgeville, Wisconsin

One farm, two cheeses. How a century of milking cows on Pleasant Ridge led to the most-awarded cheese in the country.

Our cheese is made by a small group of people grazing a unique herd of cows on a steep ridgetop farm. This is the story of our land, animals and people. The story of who we are and why we're here.

SHOP THE CHEESE
→
WHERE TO BUY

Our Story

Explore our Story

THE LAND

The Driftless Region

Pleasant Ridge sits up high in the center of Wisconsin's Driftless Region, in an area known as the Uplands. This unique pocket of the Upper Midwest was untouched by the last glacial age and thus left with its ancient karst bedrock. Hills and valleys shaped by millions of years of flowing water.

1/3

THE LAND

The Driftless Region

Ancient ridgetops like ours, too windswept for forests, instead grew into grasslands. The winds pushed piles of rich, loamy soil up onto our hills, making perfect pasture for bison, who in turn fertilized the growing grass and built carbon reserves deep into the ground. Over thousands of years, the bison, the wind and the rain built some of the finest grazing soils in the world.

2/3

THE LAND

The Driftless Region

Despite our rich soils, the first farmers struggled on these steep hills, which don't lend themselves to the plow. Farms stayed small or didn't stay at all and it wasn't until the 1990s, when our farm was planted back to perennial pasture, that it returned to its calling. Grassland supporting ruminants supporting grassland.

3/3

OUR COWS

Our Herd Is At The Center Of It All

Since our farm returned to pasture in 1994, we have maintained a closed herd, with the goal of developing cows suited to our land. Over the decades, we have crossed nine different breeds within our herd, and any cow milked here has been born and raised here.

1/3

OUR COWS

Our Herd Is At The Center Of It All

In our herd, we search for novel combinations of traits that don't exist in a single breed but are uniquely suited to our farm and our cheese.

2/3

OUR COWS

Our Herd Is At The Center Of It All

From these special cows we keep daughters, granddaughters, great-granddaughters. Their families are part of our family and they are at the center of what we do. By grazing and fertilizing, the cows sustain our soil, and by turning that grass into unique milk, they sustain us.

3/3

Our Herd

OUR CHEESE

Traditional Cheesemaking

After thousands of years of bison, a century of cows and a return to perennial pasture in the 1990s, our farm made its first cheeses in 2000. It was clear we had special pastures and a unique herd of cows, and cheese was simply a way to capture that character.

1/4

OUR CHEESE

Traditional Cheesemaking

To capture the character of our farm, we only make cheese while our cows are on pasture. Seven mornings a week, May through November, we send fresh, unpasteurized milk seventy feet underground, from the barn into the cheese vat.

2/4

Inspecting wheels

OUR CHEESE

Traditional Cheesemaking

In the spring, summer and fall, we make Pleasant Ridge Reserve, a hard cheese aged until it's ripe and ready for release the following year.

3/4

OUR CHEESE

Traditional Cheesemaking

In the fall, we make Rush Creek Reserve, a soft cheese aged for two months and sold only in November and December. Both cheeses ripen in our open-air cheese caves, where their natural rinds and our constant care bring them to their peak.

4/4

OUR PEOPLE

The People Of Uplands

Your cheese purchases also sustain us, and we are very grateful for your support. We have come to enjoy all the meaningful relationships we have with people connected to the farm. Neighbors we see once a week, distant customers we talk to once a year, and everyone in between.

1/2

OUR PEOPLE

The People Of Uplands

THE PROCESS

Our cheese is our pasture, distilled.

Land

It all begins with pasture

Each day's batch of cheese begins as the 10 acres of fresh pasture the cows grazed the day before. Our cows are rotated to new pastures twice a day, after each milking, and won't return to a field for 30–45 days, until it's had time to regrow.

Herd

Cows turn pasture into milk

Our cows transform that 10 acres of pasture into 8,000 lbs of milk, which flows from the barn into the cheese vat via an underground pipe.

Make

We turn milk into cheese

In the cheese vat, this 8,000 lbs of milk becomes 800 lbs of cheese. The fresh wheels look round and perfect but they enter the caves almost flavorless. Full of potential that will only be revealed with time.

Finish

Aging turns cheese into the best version of itself

This 800 lbs of cheese leaves the caves months later as 675 lbs. This is the final distillation of flavor, which began with pasture turning into milk, and milk into cheese. Like cooking down a stock, flavors concentrate as the cheeses dry down, revealing more and more of their core character until, at the right moment, we send them out into the world.

Timeline

Our History

HOW IT ALL BEGAN

1994

The Gingrich and Patenaude families buy the farm, convert it from row crops to perennial pasture and start rotational grazing.

FIRST BATCHES

2000

Mike Gingrich makes the first batches of Pleasant Ridge Reserve, an original cheese inspired by alpage Beaufort and Gruyère.

SHOT OUT OF A CANNON

2001

In its debut year, Pleasant Ridge is awarded Best of Show by the American Cheese Society.

A SECOND NATIONAL TITLE

2003

Pleasant Ridge is awarded Best of Show by the US Cheese Championships, making it the only cheese to win both national competitions.

A REPEAT WIN

2005

Pleasant Ridge is awarded Best of Show by the American Cheese Society for the second time.

THREE-TIME CHAMPION

2010

Pleasant Ridge is awarded Best of Show by the American Cheese Society for the third time, making it the only cheese to achieve this honor three times.

RUSH CREEK RESERVE DEBUT

2010

Rush Creek Reserve debut is covered by the New York Times, who calls it “fluent and satiny, with hints of smoke and pork.”

ONE GENERATION TO THE NEXT

2014

Longtime employees Andy Hatch and Scott Mericka buy the farm from the Gingrich and Patenaude families, succeeding their mentors.

LOOKING AHEAD

2025

Scott retires; Andy and Caitlin become sole owners and rebuild the creamery.

Soft-ripened · Autumn release

Rush Creek Reserve

Produced only in the fall, when our cows start to transition from from summer pasture to winter hay. For a few weeks each year, we tap into this vein of rich milk to create a limited amount of these soft, decadent cheeses. Modeled after Vacherin Mont d'Or, another highly seasonal cheese from France, Rush Creek Reserve has developed a loyal following in this country as a centerpiece for year-end gatherings.

Each cheese is wrapped in spruce bark, which gives shape to the cheese and imparts a subte, woodsy flavor. At its peak, Rush Creek Reserve is soft and custard-like, and it shines when served with a spoon and heaped onto a crusty baguette or drizzled over roasted vegetables.

Before serving Rush Creek, bring the cheese to room temp or warm it gently in an oven. When using an oven, remove the paper wrapping and either wrap the cheese in tin foil or cover it in a ceramic crock. Place the cheese in a 225-degree oven for approximately 15 minutes, or until the entire cheese becomes soft and warm.

Use a knife to cut around the perimeter of the cheese, just above the bark. Lift off the rind and scoop out the soft interior with a spoon. The rich, savory flavors are deep but delicate, and pair nicely with cured meats, roasted root vegetables and off-dry white wines. Storage and serving instructions are included with each order.

The label on each cheese shows the date by which it should be eaten. Typically, this "serve-by" date is 5-6 weeks from the date of shipment. For example, cheeses shipped in mid-November will have "serve-by" dates in late December or early January. Each cheese weighs approximately 12 ounces.

CARE & SERVICE

Storage & Serving

Keep refrigerated at 38–42°F. Bring to room temperature before serving. Pleasant Ridge Reserve can be stored for several weeks but is at its peak within a couple of weeks of its receiving date. Rush Creek Reserve is meant to be enjoyed as a young cheese and should be consumed by the best-by date printed on the label of the wheel.
